explanation: Source file naming conventions in C++ involve using specific suffixes to indicate that a file contains C++ code, which helps compilers and build systems process it correctly. In real-world programming, consistent naming is a best practice to ensure portability across different compilers and environments. For example, using .cpp is common with GCC and Clang, while .cc might be preferred in some Unix-based systems. This convention aids in project organization, especially in larger codebases, by making it easy to identify C++ files. Common pitfalls include using an incorrect suffix, which can lead to files being ignored during compilation or causing build errors; to avoid this, always check your compiler's documentation and adopt a project-wide standard. In practice, this pattern promotes maintainability and collaboration in teams.
code_example:
// Common C++ Source Implementation Files
widget_utils.cpp
main_program.cc
legacy_code.cxx    // Less common suffix

// Common C++ Header (Interface) Files
MyInterface.h      // Standard, often used for C compatibility
MyInterface.hpp    // C++ specific (preferred practice)

// Specialized C++ Extensions
templates.tpp      // Explicit template definitions
widget.ipp         // Internal implementation details (inlines)
